 Madhya Pradesh Diwali Air Pollution | Gwalior, Indore & Bhopal AQI High
 Gwalior records worst air quality, green Bhopal in red zone: AQI high in 5 cities ahead of Diwali, including Indore, Ujjain and Mandideep
 Bhopal 1 day ago 
 Copy link 
 The air quality in several cities of Madhya Pradesh has deteriorated even before Diwali. Gwalior is the most polluted city. The AQI was recorded at above 300 at three monitoring stations there.
 Bhopal's air has also become polluted. An AQI of 261 was recorded at the capital's Paryavaran Parisar, which falls in the Poor category. PM2.5 is the primary pollutant there.
 Besides Gwalior and Bhopal, the air quality in Indore, Ujjain and Mandideep has also deteriorated. The AQI was recorded at 233 in Indore, 229 in Ujjain and 251 in Mandideep.
 Find out about the condition in five cities of MP 
 Bhopal - Pollution-related problems worsening 
 Air quality is also a cause for concern in the capital, Bhopal. An AQI of 183 was recorded in TT Nagar and 141 in Eidgah Hills. PM 2.5 is the primary pollutant in both areas. However, the air here is in the Moderate category. This means fine-particle pollution was recorded as the main pollutant at all three monitoring stations in the capital.
 Gwalior's air is the worst, with AQI above 300 at all three stations 
 Gwalior has the worst air quality. An AQI of 348 was recorded in Deendayal Nagar, 334 in Maharaj Bada and 316 in City Centre. The air in all three areas is in the Very Poor category. However, the AQI did not cross 400 at any monitoring station in the state. This means the air is not in the Severe category anywhere.
 Pollution from both fine and coarse dust particles has increased in Gwalior. PM2.5 is the primary pollutant in Deendayal Nagar and City Centre, while PM10 levels are higher in Maharaj Bada. This means Deendayal Nagar has the highest PM2.5 level, while Maharaj Bada leads in PM10.
 Air quality also poor in Mandideep, Indore and Ujjain 
 Pollution levels have also risen in Mandideep, an industrial area near Bhopal. An AQI of 251 was recorded in the Sector-D Industrial Area. PM10 is the primary pollutant there.
 The AQI in Chhoti Gwaltoli, Indore, stood at 233. PM10 levels are higher there as well. In Mahashweta Nagar, Ujjain, an AQI of 229 was recorded, with PM2.5 as the primary pollutant.
 Besides, AQI at Suryakiran Bhavan (NCL) in Singrauli stood at 206. PM 10 was the main pollutant there. Air at all these locations was recorded in the Poor category.
 Pollution levels are not the same across all areas of Indore. The air in Chhoti Gwaltoli is in the Poor category. Meanwhile, AQI was recorded at 188 in Magoda Nagar and 172 in the Residency Area. The air in both these locations is in the Moderate category.
 AQI in the Airport Area stood at 101, with PM 10 as the pollutant. In contrast, AQI at Regional Park was recorded at just 48, with PM 2.5 as the pollutant, placing it in the Good category. According to the available data, this is the lowest AQI in the state.
 Now, find out the situation in other cities of MP 
 Air quality Moderate in Jabalpur, Sagar and other cities 
 Air quality at all four monitoring stations in Jabalpur was recorded in the Moderate category. AQI was 164 at Marhatal, 131 at Gupteshwar, 108 at Suhagi and 74 at Govind Bhavan Colony.
 In Sagar, the AQI was recorded at 154 in Civil Lines and 80 in Deendayal Nagar. Meanwhile, the AQI was 197 in Gol Bazaar, Katni; 162 at Bhopal Chauraha, Dewas; and 167 in the Sector-2 industrial area of Pithampur. NO2 was recorded as the primary pollutant in Shastri Nagar, Ratlam, where the AQI was 132.
 Among the areas with lower pollution levels, the AQI was recorded at 59 in Shrivastava Colony, Damoh; 61 in Sahilara, Maihar; and 70 in Bandhavgarh Colony, Satna. All these areas fall in the Satisfactory category. The air in Sagar's Deendayal Nagar was also in this category, with an AQI of 80.
 Gwalior leads in PM 2.5 and PM 10 pollution 
 Among the major pollutants, the highest PM 2.5 level was recorded at 348 in Deendayal Nagar, Gwalior. This was followed by 316 at City Centre, Gwalior, and 261 at Paryavaran Parisar, Bhopal.
 In the case of PM 10, Maharaj Bada in Gwalior recorded the highest level. The AQI there was 334. This was followed by 251 in Mandideep, 233 in Chhoti Gwaltoli, Indore, and 206 in Singrauli.
 Among gaseous pollutants, NO2 was recorded as the primary pollutant in Shastri Nagar, Ratlam. The AQI there was 132. However, the available data is not sufficient for a city-wise comparison of gaseous pollution.
 Understand the difference between PM 2.5 and PM 10 
 PM 2.5 refers to extremely small dust and pollution particles present in the air. They are 2.5 micrometres or smaller in size. They are so fine that they can travel deep into the lungs with the breath. Some particles can also enter the bloodstream.
 Smoke from vehicles and factories, waste burning and stubble burning are the main sources of PM 2.5. Rising PM 2.5 levels can increase the risk of respiratory and heart-related diseases.
 PM 10 refers to dust and pollution particles present in the air that are 10 micrometres or smaller in size. These include road dust, soil carried into the air by construction work, cement and particles released by factories.
 They can reach the nose, throat and lungs through breathing. They are larger than PM 2.5, but in high concentrations they can also harm health. Dust flying on roads, construction work and the movement of vehicles are the main causes of rising PM 10 levels.
